focus: firing arc (TryFindNewTarget override, Tick clamp, OrderAttack/Fire rejection), WeaponArtCentroid render-texture readback and centroid math vs DrawEquipmentAiming, settings apply/defaults timing
diffSource: since build 3 (2026-10-06T16:44:53Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Range setting is not reapplied to a mount that was off-map (minified) when settings changed
findings.detail: MountSettings.Apply only calls Notify_SettingsChanged on buildings spawned on a map. A mount that is uninstalled (it has a minifiedDef) keeps its gun and its cloned VerbProperties. On reinstall, SpawnSetup -> PrepareMountedWeapon skips the rescale because appliedProps already contains each verb's props, so the old range stays until the save is reloaded. In SpawnSetup, after PrepareMountedWeapon(), set appliedProps[i].range = baseRanges[i] * Ext.rangeMultiplier (the loop already in Notify_SettingsChanged).

findings.title: Apply() saves every mount's XML values into the settings, so later XML or balance-patch changes are ignored
findings.detail: Apply calls TuningFor(def) for every mount at startup (MountSettings.cs:100). TuningFor copies Defaults into `tunings` when the mount has no entry (MountSettings.cs:64-70). The next WriteSettings (on settings-window close) saves all of them, so after one visit to the settings window, a mod update or another mod's patch to rangeMultiplier, warmupFactor or ShootingAccuracyTurret no longer takes effect for that player. That contradicts the class comment that a balance patch is respected. One change: in Apply, read tunings.TryGetValue(...) and fall back to Defaults[def.defName] without inserting; leave the inserting TuningFor for the settings UI in DoMounts.

findings.title: ArtCentroidWorld leaves out the recoil angle that DrawEquipmentAiming adds
findings.detail: DrawEquipmentAiming adds EquipmentUtility.Recoil's angleOffset to the rotation after the mesh choice. The centroid offset is computed without it, so during recoil the art turns about a point slightly off its centroid. The error is about |centroid| x recoil angle, a few hundredths of a cell. Only visible on strongly off-centre art such as the minigun.

findings.title: Arc is checked only when a burst starts; later shots can follow a target out of the arc
findings.detail: Fire() checks InArc once before TryStartCastOn. Base Tick returns early while the verb is Bursting, so later shots in a burst can track a target past the arc edge. The drawn rotation stays clamped by the Tick clamp, so the shots and the gun's drawn aim can disagree for the rest of the burst.

findings.title: Tick clears forcedTarget without resetting warmup or currentTarget
findings.detail: Vanilla's ResetForcedTarget also zeroes burstWarmupTicksLeft. Here currentTargetInt keeps pointing at the target that left the arc, so the gun sits at the arc edge until the warmup ends and Fire() calls ResetTargeting. It recovers by itself; calling ResetTargeting() here, as Notify_SettingsChanged does, would drop the target straight away.

findings.title: One shared DrawField cache rebuilds every frame when several mounts with different facings are selected
findings.detail: The cells/cachedCenter/cachedRot cache is static and shared by every selected mount and the placement ghost. Two selected mounts make it rebuild (2r+1)^2 cells per mount per frame. With a 2x range multiplier r can be about 60. That costs some performance but causes no errors.

findings.title: MountExtension's per-def destruction fields are no longer read
findings.detail: Destroy now reads MountSettings.Get.maxWeaponDamage and coreLossChance. MountExtension.maxWeaponDamageWhenKilled and coreLossChanceWhenKilled are still declared but nothing reads them, so a def or another mod's patch that sets them is silently ignored.

findings.title: Slider snaps and clamps values on every draw, so viewing a mount tab changes off-grid values
findings.detail: Slider sets value = Clamp(RoundTo(l.Slider(...), roundTo), min, max) on every repaint, not only when dragged. An XML or patched value off the 0.05 grid, or below the 1.0 range minimum, is rewritten just by opening the tab, then saved on close. Your own defs' values all sit on the grids, so this only bites other mods' patches. Only writing back when l.Slider's result differs from the input would avoid it.

findings.title: Settings refresh only reaches colonist-owned mounts
findings.detail: Apply loops listerBuildings.AllBuildingsColonistOfClass<Building_WeaponMount>(), which walks allBuildingsColonist only. A mount owned by another faction keeps its old range clones (appliedProps) until reload. Iterating map.listerThings for the def, or allBuildingsNonColonist as well, would cover them.

findings.title: Arc changes apply mid-drag; range, aim and accuracy apply only on window close
findings.detail: ArcFor is read live by Building_WeaponMount.Arc (Building_WeaponMount.cs:73), so arc slider changes affect targeting while the window is still open. Range, aim and accuracy reach the defs only through WriteSettings → Apply on PreClose, and that is also when out-of-arc forced targets are reset. It is consistent once the window closes, so this is harmless; worth knowing if someone reports the arc changing before the rest.

findings.title: MountExtension.coreLossChanceWhenKilled / maxWeaponDamageWhenKilled are now dead XML fields
findings.detail: Building_WeaponMount now reads MountSettings.Get.coreLossChance and maxWeaponDamage (Building_WeaponMount.cs:377, 391). Nothing reads the per-def extension fields any more, so an XML patch that sets them silently does nothing. No def in this mod sets them.
